html:
SMTO-SCH-0005 — The schedule needs a time as well as a date

GUID: bb30f623-03dd-4e31-bd43-dbff6526a953
Slug: schedule-timestamp-must-include-a-date-and-time
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • A date was given for this schedule but no clock time, so SMTO doesn't know when on that day to run it. The schedule wasn't saved, and nothing ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the schedule editor, fill in the At field with the time of day you want, next to the Starts date. A date alone doesn't say what hour the schedule should run.
  2. If you asked SMTO in a message, ask again and include the time, for example "on October 9 at 9:00 AM". SMTO won't guess a time of day for you.
  3. Before you save, read the summary line under the schedule settings. It shows the date and time SMTO will use, so you can confirm both are there.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and shows a next run with both the date and the time you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't resubmit the same date-only value.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schedule time resolution rejected a timestamp with no date/time separator (a date without a clock time); this is normally reported wrapped as the ISO date-time error.

What this means

  • A date without a clock time cannot specify the schedule’s run instant. This source diagnostic is normally wrapped by the ISO date-and-time error. It does not indicate a failed scheduled action.

Why this can happen

  • The timestamp lacks the date-and-time separator checked by resolve_at.

How to diagnose it

  • Check whether the submitted timestamp contains only a date. Include a time and, when needed, an explicit UTC offset.

How to fix it

  • Supply both the date and the clock time in next_run_at (for example 2026-10-09T14:30:00 with the intended offset or time zone) and check the schedule preview before saving. resolve_at in events/timing.py requires a 'T' or space separator.
  • Supply both the intended date and clock time, then inspect the schedule preview before saving.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The full timestamp parses and the preview shows the intended instant.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • resolve_at rejects input lacking a date/time separator and wraps it in the ISO timestamp identity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
